 IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR ANTICIPATORY BAIL) NO. 9706  of 2025  ==========================================================

 Appearance:

sentences.text: Learned APP waives service of notice of Rule for and on behalf of the respondent - State of Gujarat.

[1.0] By way of the present application under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short "BNSS"), the applicant accused has prayed to release him on anticipatory bail in the event of his arrest in connection with the FIR being C.R. No.11210067250170 of 2025 registered with Saroli Police Station, District Surat for the offences punishable under Sections 420,
409 and 120(B) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
[2.0] Learned advocate for the applicant submits that the applicant has nothing to do with the offence and has been falsely enroped in the offence.
He is Proprietor of Krishna Fabrics and contacted the complainant through one broker Saiyed.
The transaction between the applicant and complainant was good initially.
Thereafter, the applicant purchased the goods through broker and payment was made to the broker, who has misappropriated the amount.

Even perusing the allegation, it appears that cheques were issued which were dishonored and to recover the amount, complaint is filed with ulterior motive.
Hence, nothing remains to be recovered or discovered from the present applicant and therefore, custodial interrogation at this stage is not necessary.
Besides, the applicant is available during the course of investigation and will not flee from justice.
In view of the above, the applicant may be granted anticipatory bail.

[3.0] Learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing on behalf of the respondent - State has opposed grant of anticipatory bail on the ground that applicant is proprietor of Krishna Fabrics and he approached the complainant and received goods worth Rs.17,86,503/- and had to pay the said amount within 45 days for which he issued 16 cheques which got dishonored.
Therefore, custodial interrogation is required and even the applicant is having past antecedent.
Hence, as custodial interrogation of the applicant is required, he has requested to dismiss the present application.

[4.0] Having heard the learned advocate for the parties and perusing the investigation papers, it is equally incumbent upon the Court to exercise its discretion judiciously, cautiously and strictly in compliance with the basic principles laid down in a plethora of decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court on the point.

It is well settled that, among other circumstances, the factors to be borne in mind while considering an application for bail are (i) the nature and gravity of the accusation; (ii) the antecedents of the applicant including the fact as to whether he has previously undergone imprisonment on conviction by a Court in respect of any cognizable offence; (iii) the possibility of the applicant to flee from justice; and (iv) where the accusation has been made with NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/9706/2025 ORDER DATED: 09/05/2025 undefined the object of injuring or humiliating the applicant by having him so arrested.
Though at the stage of granting bail an elaborate examination of evidence and detailed reasons touching the merit of the case, which may prejudice the accused, should be avoided.
I have considered the following aspects.
(1) Offence is not punishable with life imprisonment or death penalty and triable by the Court of JMFC;

As per the recent decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Rikhab Birani & Anr. vs. State of Uttar Pradesh & Anr.
reported in 2025 INSC 512 as well as in the case of Lalit Chaturvedi and Others vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Another reported in 2024 SCC OnLine SC 171, any effort to settle civil disputes and claims, which do not involve any criminal offence, by applying pressure through criminal Rajeshkumar Ramgopal Sharma vs State Of Gujarat on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153059386/
2 prosecution should be deprecated and discouraged.
[5.0] Considering the aforesaid aspects and the law laid down by the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/9706/2025 ORDER DATED: 09/05/2025 undefined Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre vs. State of Maharashtra and Ors. reported in (2011) 1 SCC 6941,
wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court reiterated the law laid down by the Constitution Bench in the case of Shri Gurubaksh Singh Sibbia & Ors. reported in (1980) 2 SCC 665 and also the decision in the case of Sushila Aggarwal v. State (NCT of Delhi) reported in (2020) 5 SCC 1, I am inclined to allow the present application.
